subject: Data exportability and subprocessor 'escape hatch' — DPIA and audit scope
messages:
From: Claire Barnes <claire.b@clearline.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal - Clearline <legal@clearline.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Data exportability and subprocessor 'escape hatch' — DPIA and audit scope

Hi Hannah / Jonas,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're starting to pull together the DPIA and procurement packet for Clearline Financial's vendor review and have a couple of items we need from Redwood to close our checklist: 

- A sample Article 30 processing register extract showing fields you capture and the exporters/importer mappings (we need at least one CSV extract we can include in our packet).
- An excerpt of KMS/audit logs showing customer key rotation and access events (redacted is fine) — our privacy office needs to validate key separation and access controls.
- Clarification on your subprocessors, specifically: any offshore data-processing subprocessors used for inference or logging, and an "escape hatch"/transition plan in case we require onshore-only processing after go-live.
- Confirmation of your support for DPIA evidence (attending a 60-min workshop with our privacy team and providing a short written summary).

Can you confirm what you can share by next Thursday (7 Dec)? If you have a template or an internal playbook for handing Art. 28/30 artifacts to customers, that would speed things up.

Also looping in Tom Alvarez from Procurement (tom.alvarez@procurex.com) who will own contract redlines.

Best,
Claire
Claire Barnes
Head of Privacy Operations | Clearline Financial
Attachment: requirements_checklist_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Barnes <claire.b@clearline.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Legal - Clearline <legal@clearline.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 12:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Data exportability and subprocessor 'escape hatch' — DPIA and audit scope

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear list. We can provide everything you've requested; outline below and proposed timing: 

- Art.30 register extract: attached redwood_art30_sample.csv (contains processing categories, legal bases, subprocessors mapped to locations; PII redacted).
- KMS/audit excerpt: attached kms_audit_log_excerpt.pdf (we've redacted customer identifiers; shows rotation events and admin accesses).
- Subprocessor map: attached subprocessor_map_v2.xlsx (current as of 2026-11-28). Rows flagged as "inference" or "logging" indicate primary function and region.
- DPIA support: happy to run the 60-min workshop with our Privacy & Security lead (Jonas) + provide a 1-page written summary outlining controls and mitigation options. Proposed dates: 7 Dec (afternoon CET) or 9 Dec (morning CET).

Escape hatch / onshore-only plan: high level — we support (1) routing by policy to onshore-only capacity for regulated accounts, (2) pre-provisioning of private Dedicated pools in EU regions, and (3) an operational migration playbook we can share. That playbook includes timeline estimates (2–6 weeks depending on committed capacity), required procurement steps, and data export mechanics. We'll attach the playbook excerpt in the follow-up if helpful.

Next steps:
- I'll drop the three attachments to you now (see attached).
- Jonas / Marissa — can you confirm the onshore provisioning timelines and the playbook excerpt we can share publicly (redacted)?

Cheers,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Manager, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_art30_sample.csv; kms_audit_log_excerpt.pdf; subprocessor_map_v2.xlsx

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:18:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Data exportability and subprocessor 'escape hatch' — DPIA and audit scope

Hannah — quick internal note. For Clearline's ask:

- Onshore provisioning: confirmed 2–4 weeks to spin up a Dedicated EU pool if they sign reserved capacity; if they want a temporary routing policy to onshore hosts without a commit, we can do 5–7 business days with burst capacity (ops approval required).
- KMS logs: security can provide 90-day rotation + admin access events; full immutable audit ledger is available for enterprise customers (longer retention is add-on). Need Legal to approve redaction language for the sample.
- Playbook excerpt: Marissa, can you pull the "migration-playbook-excerpt.pdf" we use for procurement and remove internal runbooks? Send to Hannah for customer delivery.

I'll also create a short bullet summary that maps each Clearline checklist item to a Redwood artifact (Art.30 sample -> art30 csv; KMS -> kms excerpt; escape hatch -> migration playbook; DPIA workshop -> Jonas as attendee). Assigning PRIV-452 to track.

Jonas
Director, Applied Privacy & Controls | Redwood Inference

From: Claire Barnes <claire.b@clearline.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@procurex.com>, Legal - Clearline <legal@clearline.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Data exportability and subprocessor 'escape hatch' — DPIA and audit scope

Hi Hannah / Jonas — got the attachments, thank you — the sample Art.30 CSV and KMS excerpt look good for our DPIA packet. A couple of quick clarifications before we move to scheduling the workshop: 

1) For the KMS excerpt, can you add a short footnote that describes retention windows for audit logs and whether event exports are permitted for customer auditors?
2) For the subprocessor_map_v2.xlsx: rows marked as "offshore" — can you list whether they ever receive decrypted customer payloads or only encrypted tensors/metadata? That distinction matters for our legal team.

If you can add those two notes by EOD Thursday 9 Dec, we'll take the packet to the privacy board and aim to confirm the workshop date. Tom — procurement, please let us know contract timeline constraints; we may request a temporary routing policy during review.

Thanks — Claire
Attachment: clearline_requirements_v1_filled.pdf (internal checklist)
